display.title: Tanya Shiur 39: Tanya Chapter 28, Foreign Thoughts During Prayer (Chanukah)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur on Tanya chapter 28: what to do when stray thoughts come during davening and learning, with a story of Rabbi Meir of Premishlan and a Chanukah talk.
display.summary_long: Shiur 39 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, recorded during Chanukah. It studies Tanya chapter 28. From the outside a beinoni and a tzaddik look the same, since both learn and daven and never sin, but the beinoni still has an animal soul that sends foreign thoughts, especially while he davens or learns. The Alter Rebbe teaches not to be troubled by them: push them away at once, and do not try to 'elevate' them, which belongs only to tzaddikim. The story of Rabbi Meir of Premishlan, who walked up an icy mountain to the mikvah without slipping because he was 'tied above', shows the point, as told by the Frierdiker Rebbe. The shiur continues: the thoughts come because two souls are wrestling, so they are a sign of real prayer, not a reason for sadness; serve Hashem with great joy; ignore the yetzer hara like a heckler you do not answer; and when it is hard, ask Hashem for mercy like a father for his child. A closing talk retells a teaching of the Rebbe from Chanukah and Yud-Tes Kislev: after his release, the Alter Rebbe drank a glass of tea in the home of an opponent rather than give offense.
display.lesson: Stray thoughts during davening are no reason for sadness: push them away at once, strengthen yourself with joy, and ask Hashem for help.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 28: the beinoni and foreign thoughts
segments.summary: A beinoni looks like a tzaddik from outside; stray thoughts during prayer must be pushed away at once, and elevating them is only for tzaddikim.

segments.title: Rabbi Meir of Premishlan and the icy mountain
segments.summary: Rabbi Meir walks straight up an icy slope to the mikvah; two scoffers who try to copy him slip, and learn that one who is tied above does not fall.

segments.title: Serving with joy while the two souls wrestle
segments.summary: Foreign thoughts are a sign of the battle between the two souls, not of bad prayer; ignore them like a heckler and ask Hashem for mercy when it is hard.

segments.title: Repeated passage
segments.summary: A stretch of the previous few minutes is heard a second time (unedited recording).

segments.title: The Rebbe's Chanukah talk: the Alter Rebbe and the glass of tea
segments.summary: Brought by mistake to an opponent's home after his release, the Alter Rebbe still drank the tea he was offered, teaching not to wound another Jew even with a word.
